title: Drug Behaviour Imaging on Phenix
author: Ida Barlow
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfgvjjw6
materials: Bleach synchronisation of C. elegans by Ida Barlow

steps.title: Prepare drug solution
steps.instruction: Identify each drug, calculate a 1000‑fold stock amount, weigh the required amount in a fume hood using an analytical balance into a labeled Eppendorf tube, add solvent (e.g., DMSO) to reach the calculated concentration, close the tube, and vortex at setting 10 for 30 seconds (repeat longer vortexing if needed) until fully dissolved.

substeps.instruction: Identify drugs and ensure they are correctly labeled and handled.
Calculate the required weight/volume for a 1000‑fold stock (e.g., mM for desired µM final concentration).
Weigh the calculated amount of powdered compound (or measure liquid) in a fume hood with an analytical balance into an Eppendorf tube labeled with the compound name and intended final concentration.
Add the appropriate volume of solvent (e.g., DMSO) to achieve the calculated concentration; close the tube lid.
Vortex the tube at setting 10 for 30 seconds; if the compound is not fully dissolved, vortex longer and repeat until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Select and label imaging plates
steps.instruction: Choose fresh unseeded 35 mm NGM plates no older than three days, inspect each for an even agar surface, and label the side of each plate with the compound name, concentration, and date using the provided spreadsheet template.

substeps.instruction: Select the required number of 35 mm NGM plates that are ≤ 3 days old.
Inspect each plate to confirm a uniform agar level; discard any uneven plates.
Label the side of each plate with the compound name, concentration, and date according to Phenix_template.xlsx.

steps.title: Apply drug to plates and dry
steps.instruction: In a flow hood, pipette 50 µL sterile water onto the centre of each agar plate, then add 3.5 µL of the prepared drug solution, and allow the plates to dry with lids off for approximately 30 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Place the labeled plates in a flow hood.
Apply 50 µL sterile water to the centre of the agar to aid drug spreading.
Immediately add 3.5 µL of the appropriate drug solution (confirm correct compound and concentration).
Leave the plates with lids off in the flow hood to dry for about 30 minutes.

steps.title: Seed plates with OP50 bacteria
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:10 OP50 suspension in M9, vortex until no pellet remains, then seed each dried plate with 50 µL of this suspension; replace lids on any plates that begin to overdry.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve a Falcon tube of OP50 from the fridge.
Vortex on setting 10 until the pellet is fully dissolved and no clumps are visible.
Dilute the OP50 1:10 with M9 solution.
Pipette 50 µL of the diluted OP50 onto the centre of each dried drug plate.
If some plates dry before others, replace their lids to prevent overdrying.

steps.title: Overnight incubation of plates
steps.instruction: Leave the seeded plates overnight at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Label plates for imaging run
steps.instruction: Identify plates according to the experimental Excel template and label each with the set number, rig position, and add a black‑dot annotation as indicated.

steps.title: Refeed L1s to young adults
steps.instruction: Refeed L1 larvae to obtain young adult worms on the day of tracking.

steps.title: Transfer worms onto drug plates
steps.instruction: For each set, pick 10 synchronized young adult worms and place them onto each drug‑treated plate within 10 minutes to ensure equivalence.

steps.title: Acclimate worms before imaging
steps.instruction: After 3 h 30 min, transfer the 10 worms to the imaging plates and let them acclimate for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Image worms and save as HDF5
steps.instruction: Image the worms for 15 minutes at 25 fps, saving the data in .hdf5 file format.

steps.title: Transfer image files to server
steps.instruction: Copy the .hdf5 image files to the analysis server.
